source_refs.note: Topic 7.2.1, printed pages 146-147, as printed: Sample Problem 7.1 (its instantaneous-rate line is printed without the data it needs) and Quick Check 7.2.

blocks.title: Instantaneous rate
blocks.text: The rate at any one instant during the interval is called the instantaneous rate.

blocks.title: Average rate
blocks.text: Whereas the average rate of reaction is defined as, “The rate of reaction between two specific time intervals or the rate over a time period”.

The average rate and instantaneous rate are equal for only one instant in any time interval. At first, the instantaneous rate is higher than the average rate. At the end of the interval the instantaneous rate becomes lower than the average rate.

blocks.title: Sample Problem 7.1
blocks.problem: The reaction for the formation of ammonia in Haber process is: N₂(aq) + 3H₂(g) → 2NH₃(g). i. Calculate the instantaneous rate after 1.0 min. ii. What is the average rate of production of ammonia for the system, between 1.0 and 4.0 minutes?
steps: The instantaneous rate at 1.0 min can be calculated as
Instantaneous Rate = ΔC/Δt = 2.7 mol dm⁻³ / 1 min = 2.7 mol dm⁻³ min⁻¹
If the concentration of ammonia is 3.5 mol dm⁻³ after 1.0 min and 6.2 mol dm⁻³ after 4.0 minutes?
ΔC = Δ[NH₃] = (6.2 − 3.5) mol dm⁻³ ; ΔC = 2.7 mol dm⁻³
Rate of formation of NH₃ = ΔC/Δt = Δ[NH₃]/Δt = 2.7 mol dm⁻³ / 3 min = 0.90 mol dm⁻³ min⁻¹
blocks.answer: The rate of production of NH₃ gas over the given time interval is 0.90 mol dm³ min¹.
book_errors: 2.7 mol dm⁻³ / 1 min = 2.7 mol dm⁻³ min⁻¹

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: Nitrogen in the Haber process is a gas: N₂(g), not N₂(aq). The instantaneous rate cannot be found this way: 2.7 mol dm⁻³ is the change between 1.0 and 4.0 min, and dividing it by 1 min gives neither the instantaneous nor the average rate. The instantaneous rate at 1.0 min needs the slope of the tangent to the concentration-time curve at 1.0 min, which the book does not give. In the last line the unit has lost its minus signs: the average rate is 0.90 mol dm⁻³ min⁻¹.

items: The reaction of hydrogen and iodine to make hydrogen iodide at a particular temperature, H₂(g) + I₂(g) → 2HI(g) was studied at various times. At 100.0 s after the start of the reaction, the iodine concentration had fallen from 0.010 mol dm⁻³ to 0.0080 mol dm⁻³. What is the average rate of reaction during this period?
